newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called to open flat to firmer.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called to open flat to firmer.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were called to open flat to 5 cents higher Thursday and products were called to open flat to 0.10 cent firmer, traders said.
IPE Brent was a touch higher at 1305 GMT after a test of its upper levels failed to push above resistance.

News that Turkish troops had moved deeper into Iraq was having little impact on Brent trading, despite the fact it managed to spark a last-minute shortcovering rally on NYMEX at the close on Wednesday, New York traders said.
Thursday's pre-open talk included the Turkish news, but only casually, with more traders focused on chart points.
"If we don't get out of the box early and retest last week's highs, we could be in for a real pullback," one analyst said. "I mean a real pullback - 60, 80 or a hundred points."
The market lacked any news that might move the products, which themselves were expected to mostly track crude.
Still, some traders have held out the last bit of hope that some sort of summer driving-season rally in unleaded gasoline futures could materialize before the end of May.
Wednesday's low of $21.46 in July crude was considered a minor test of intermediate support at $21.50, but the stronger support level was seen at the $21.13/16 range, dealers said.
